topic: Gap Locks Turn Concurrent Inserts Into Deadlock Traps
postText:
High-throughput writes crashed our admission pipeline during peak triage hours. No shared row updates, no table locks, yet database threads dropped into deadlocks instantly.

In healthcare IT, thousands of concurrent transactions fire during morning shifts: bed assignments, visit logs, and billing checks. Developers expect deadlocks when two transactions fight over the exact same row. But our telemetry showed transactions deadlocking on distinct row IDs.

The real culprit was InnoDB Next-Key Locking under default REPEATABLE READ isolation.

When queries filter on non-unique secondary indexes or scan ranges before an insert, the database locks the index record and the entire gap preceding it. Two concurrent transactions inserting different records into the same gap obtain shared gap locks, then mutually wait for exclusive insert intention locks. Total freeze. Deadlock detector steps in. Immediate transaction rollback.

How we fixed the deadlock storm:
1. Transitioned OLTP workloads from REPEATABLE READ to READ COMMITTED with row-based replication, removing phantom protection gap locks.
2. Enforced deterministic resource sorting across all business services—always acquire row updates in ascending primary key order.
3. Replaced range-based check queries with strict unique point lookups.

Have you ever debugged phantom deadlocks where transactions failed without updating the same record? How did you isolate the lock contention?

If this breakdown helped clarify DB locking internals, like, drop your experience in the comments, and share this post with your engineering team.
